New
Senior Officer, Carbon Finance
Indonesia
INTRODUCTION TO GGGI

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page.
Position Grade: G9
Position Scale: Country Scale
Contract Duration: 31 December 2028
Application Deadline: Shown in the bottom of the page
Position Summary

Carbon Finance Senior Officer will be based in Jakarta, Indonesia and lead the overall implementation of GGGI Indonesia’s carbon finance portfolio. The Senior Officer will report to the Investment Lead of GGGI Indonesia and coordinate closely with GGGI’s global Carbon Finance Department and other carbon finance teams, both globally and across GGGI’s network of country offices. The Senior Officer will serve as the primary technical focal point for projects related to carbon finance in Indonesia, and be responsible for timely, high-quality carbon finance project delivery. The position holder will provide day-to-day technical and strategic guidance and management and liaise externally to ensure the effective delivery of carbon finance outputs and activities.
Purpose

Lead the implementation of GGGI’s carbon market and carbon finance portfolio in Indonesia, including Article 6 initiatives, ensuring effective coordination with the NACA Fund Project, under the Carbon Finance Department.

Take primary responsibility to lead and manage the implementation of the NACA Project in Indonesia, ensuring effective project planning, coordination, execution, monitoring, and reporting; overseeing delivery of project outputs and outcomes; managing engagement with government counterparts, and other key stakeholders, and ensuring alignment with GGGI’s strategic priorities and the project’s objectives.

Provide high-quality project, output and component management for designated project activities, and ensure effective, timely and efficient delivery of project results and activities in the field.Provide strategic advice in exploring new carbon market instruments, such as emission trading scheme (ETS), voluntary carbon market, and others, for specific sectors including blue economy, energy/renewable energy, waste management, agriculture, etc.

Provide high-quality technical inputs and advisory on issues related to Article 6, carbon markets, and emissions reduction trading in support country’s needs and GGGI Indonesia’s portfolio and strategic priorities more generally.

Support the ongoing development of GGGI’s carbon finance portfolio in Indonesia, with a focus on positioning the organization and its services to support Government of Indonesia’s long-term carbon finance needs across multiple instruments and sectors.
Engagement
Report directly to the Investment Lead, with matrix reporting to GGGI’s Carbon Finance Department (NACA Fund) at HQ, to ensure timely and high-quality delivery of project activities and outputs.

Support the development and application of technical knowledge of Article 6 requirements, frameworks and implementation approaches, as well as other countries best practices on the mandatory and voluntary carbon market approaches.
Develop and foster strong relationships with key government stakeholders, leading the day-to-day communication.
Serve as the primary technical and strategic counterpart to key government stakeholders, leading day-to-day engagement and supporting coordination with other sectoral ministries.

Coordinate with other organizations/development partners supporting engagement with international carbon markets in Indonesia and ensure visibility of programming related to Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and associated carbon engagements.
Maintain active flexibility through professional relations with key stakeholders to capture and integrate the changing needs of stakeholders and manage expectations.
Delivery
The candidate is expected to deliver the following:
Deliver high-quality project outputs on time and within budget that meet program objectives, donor requirements and government requirements.
Supervise the team member, including associates, junior analysts, consultants, and interns, related on carbon finance work.
Quickly absorb and apply sufficient technical knowledge on Article 6 concepts, requirements, frameworks and approaches, as well as mandatory and voluntary carbon market contexts.
Ensure quality monitoring and evaluation, timely submission of donor reports and deliverables, regularly evaluate project results, and guide project implementation to achieve maximum impact.
Assess effectiveness of project activities and recommmend improvements to meet key milestones for the program.
Ensure that experiences and best practices are documented and shared across relevant sectors in Indonesia and GGGI’s broader carbon finance work.
Plan and co-deliver capacity building events that introduce key Article 6 concepts, and other carbon market instruments and options to key government and other stakeholders.

Lead the design and implementation of mitigation activities for Article 6, in collaboration with the Government of Indonesia and private sector, in close collaboration with NACA Fund, and country team.
Explore any potential of carbon finance initiatives from other carbon market instruments, such as emission trading scheme, voluntary carbon markets, that relevant for specific sector in Indonesia.
Support and facilitate existing bilateral engagement between Government of Indonesia, and assess any potential cooperation partners.
Support the process of facilitating key agreements between government, private sector and other international partners.
Lead the planning and facilitation of key project workshops and meetings with key stakeholders in Indonesia.
Plan and organize the work of individual consultants under the project to ensure high quality and timely delivery of the outputs.
Ensure the quality of delivery of the project in a timely manner.
Uphold GGGI’s values.
Requirements
QUALIFICATION
Master’s degree relevant to climate finance, economics, finance, environmental engineering, environmental sciences, or other related disciplines.
Preferably 8 years of experience in country-level work experience, experience with climate finance, carbon market, and carbon finance are highly desirable.
Understanding of and experience in international carbon markets, the Clean Development Mechanism, emission trading scheme, voluntary carbon market, and/or Article 6 is a strong advantage.

Strong understanding and demonstrated experience in Indonesia’s energy sectors, particularly renewable energy development, energy transition policies, and the regulatory and institutional landscape in Indonesia.

Proven track record in project management, including planning, reporting, and financial management, with experience in people management considered an asset. Experience in day-to-day engagement with government ministries and agencies, ideally in developing countries.
Experience in close engagement with the private sector is a strong advantage.
Experience in organizing consultations, validation meetings, workshops and capacity building events.
Experience in stakeholder engagement and working with inter-institutional programmes.
Ability to lead and work effectively with people from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds.
Excellent English and Indonesian oral and written communication skills, including public speaking.
FUNCTIONAL
Ability to develop and maintain strong relationships with GGGI partner institutions.
Experience in policy formulation, capacity building and multi-stakeholder engagement.
Ability to understand Government policy and strategy formulation and implementation mechanisms at national and sub-national levels within a multi-sectoral and cross-sectoral context in Indonesia.
Excellent organizational and management skills and demonstrated experience in successfully mainstreaming of safeguards, gender, poverty reduction and social inclusion.
Demonstrated understanding of principles of green investment and climate financing.
Ability to manage projects that are supported by international and local consultants.
Ability to work in an organized, systematic manner, with degree of innovations and decision-making abilities.
Ability to write concise and clear reports and meeting minutes and to file them effectively and develop and maintain the GGGI database accordingly.
Ability to perform in demanding atmosphere and self-motivate to produce quality results in timely manner.
CORPORATE
Understand and actively support GGGI’s mission, vision and values.
Promote an organizational culture of trust, transparency, respect and partnership.
Excels at problem solving, asks questions and seeks support when needed, easily shares information and knowledge with others both internally as externally.
Manage emotions and stress positively, build rapport and resolves conflict easily.
Strong ability to work independently and/or remotely, while maintaining productivity.
Work Conditions
Senior Officer is an G9 grade level in GGGI’s National salary scale. Determination of base salary is subject to candidate's experience, academic background and internal equity.
GGGI provides 15% of base salary towards retirement plan/long-term savings, 27 days of annual leave, and private health insurance that covers dental and vision.

GGGI is committed to providing a work environment that is sufficiently flexible to accommodate diverse life-cycle challenges and assist Staff members to achieve a better balance between work and personal/family commitments, thus ensuring high performance, long-term productivity, and well-being of Staff members.
The chosen candidate is expected to be based in Jakarta, Indonesia, and will report to the Country Investment Lead (also based in Jakarta).
This is a national position and does not include relocation benefits.
Project Introduction

GGGI supports the Government of Indonesia (GoI) under the joint GoI-GGGI Green Indonesia Future Initiative Program (GIFT). GIFT aims to demonstrate that green investments can become the norm both for investors and planners, ultimately improving the quality of economic development for more environmental sustainability and social inclusion. Through the Program, GGGI collaborates with the Ministry of Development Planning (BAPPENAS) as program host, the Coordinating Ministry of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Forestry, PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur (“PT SMI”), Indonesia Environment Fund (IEF), and other key stakeholders.

Indonesia is one of the world’s largest climate finance markets, yet its climate investment needs continue to grow as the country strengthens its climate ambitions. According to Indonesia’s Second NDC, an estimated USD472.6 billion in investment is required across energy, agriculture, FOLU, and waste sectors for the 2030-2035 period. Mobilizing financing at this scale will require substantial private sector participation alongside public funding. The Second NDC underscores Indonesia’s commitment to strengthening international cooperation and mobilizing private climate finance, supported by policy instruments as Presidential Regulation No. 110/2025 on carbon pricing mechanisms.

In line with the objectives of GGGI’s Indonesia’s new Country Programme Framework, GGGI Indonesia has set a target to mobilize USD2 billion in cumulative climate investment commitments between 2026 and 2030. Achieving this target will require scaling up innovative climate finance solutions, with carbon finance serving as a strategic pillar for mobilizing private capital, strengthening the bankability of climate projects, and accelerating investment in Indonesia’s green transition. Through the development and implementation of a robust carbon project pipeline and portfolio through Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, emission trading systems, voluntary carbon market, GGGI Indonesia aims to unlock new sources of climate finance, facilitate investment opportunities, and generate measurable climate and sustainable development outcomes.

Child protection – GGGI is committed to child protection, irrespective of whether any specific area of work involves direct contact with children. GGGI’s Child Protection Policy is written in accordance with the Convention on the Rights of the Child.
